key_claims.claim: Exome or genome sequencing identifies pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 30% of prenatally diagnosed ACC cases after negative CMA, with yield increasing to 41% when additional phenotypic features are present.
After PGT-A euploid embryo transfer, residual confirmed aneuploidy risk at amniocentesis is approximately 0.1%, and cfDNA positive predictive value is only 12.5%.

In prenatally diagnosed closed spinal dysraphism, limited dorsal myeloschisis is the most common subtype, with prenatal-postnatal diagnostic concordance and functional outcomes now characterized at 36 months.
A multivariable model combining multiple sagittal aortic-arch parameters improves prenatal coarctation discrimination over any single echocardiographic measurement.
A genetic etiology is identified in approximately 30% of fetal intracranial hemorrhage cases that undergo comprehensive investigation.
